messages:
ash: Noticed a batch of restore failures for tenant-112 snapshots in eu-west-1. All failing with KMS "AccessDenied" or "NotFoundException" when DescribeKey is called.

vik: link to failing restore job: <https://internal.redwood/jobs/restore/7881>

marta: error from restore log: `ERROR: kms.DescribeKey: An error occurred (NotFoundException) when calling the DescribeKey operation: Key 'arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:222233334444:key/9f8e7d6c' not found`

ash: weird because that key was the dest CMK we rolled out last week. It exists in console. Could this be an org-level SCP or an account isolation change?

cloudops: I can see an org SCP applied at 02:04 UTC that restricts `kms:DescribeKey` across a subset of member accounts for compliance testing. Policy id: SCP-2026-03-22-RestrictKMSRead.

sec-bot: Alert created: ACL-2026-452 / kms-access-ops. Runbook: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/kms-access-denied

audit-svc: audit entry: 2026-03-22T02:04:11Z org:AttachPolicy policyId=SCP-2026-03-22-RestrictKMSRead actor=policymgr@security-team

vik: If SCP prevents DescribeKey, then APIs that call DescribeKey before decrypt will fail with NotFound. That explains both NotFound and AccessDenied variants.

marta: That also means restores that rely on cross-account decrypt grants will fail. We need a mitigation that doesn't require removing the SCP right away (compliance wants the test).

ash: Short-term mitigation options:
- temporarily add a KMS grant on the dest CMK for the restore role (bypasses DescribeKey? Not always)
- re-run re-encrypt pipeline but use `aws kms re-encrypt` with `--destination-key-id` by an account that has permissions (maybe a central ops account)
- fallback: import object and decrypt locally via a privileged account, then re-encrypt with dest key

cloudops: We can run a bulk `re-encrypt` from central-ops-role in account A; central-ops has an exception in the SCP. That would rewrap ciphertext to the dest key without needing the restore role to DescribeKey.

marta: For vuln triage: any chance the SCP change was exploited? risk vector: someone could have created a key with similar alias in another account and trick restore job? low but flagging for review.

sec-bot: P0 checklist created in INC-2026-452.

audit-svc: Quick query: show iam actions touching backup roles since 2026-03-20:
```
2026-03-20T23:45:01Z iam:PutRolePolicy user=ops:emily role=backup-manager policy=RestrictUpload
2026-03-21T00:12:09Z iam:DetachRolePolicy user=ops:mark role=replicator policy=LegacyReplicatorFull
```

vik: Also noticed a change in replication code that switched S3 copy to preserve SSE headers when it detected unknown dest key: fallback logic bug. That combined with SCP means objects copied with source key metadata point at a CMK that dest account can't Describe. Restore fails.

ash: Proposed remediation plan:
1) immediate: schedule central-ops re-encrypt for all objects with SSEKMSKeyId pointing to cross-account sources in last 48h.
2) create temporary grant on source keys for central-ops if needed. Log grant IDs in ticket.
3) patch replication service to force re-encrypt (`--metadata-directive REPLACE`) and add unit tests to prevent header-preserve fallback.
4) update infra policy: SCPs used for testing must include allowed `kms:DescribeKey` for service principal used by restores OR central-ops exception.
5) add detection alert: S3 object SSEKMSKeyId != expected-dest-cmk for replicated prefixes.

marta: I'll run a scan to enumerate objects with mismatched SSE headers in the `snapshots/` prefix and attach list to INC-2026-452.

cloudops: running quick re-encrypt plan now in dry-run mode for 200 objs. Using central-ops-role: `aws s3 cp s3://src-bucket/key s3://dst-bucket/key --metadata-directive REPLACE --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:eu-west-1:222233334444:key/9f8e7d6c`

sec-bot: Please remember to annotate tickets with grant IDs and expiry. Compliance requires non-retirable grants to be documented.

vik: For long-term: we'll add an IaC policy check that prevents pushing SCPs that block `kms:DescribeKey` for service principals (or flagging them). Also add a pre-deploy gating job that runs a synthetic restore to a canary tenant.

marta: Also propose tagging keys with `managed-by: replication-service` and `prod: true` so SCPs can be scoped safely.

ash: action items: marta (object scan + list), cloudops (execute re-encrypt + provide grant IDs), vik (replication patch + IaC gate), audit-svc (collect audit trail for SCP change and role policy edits).

cloudops: dry-run re-encrypt succeeded for sample. moving to actual. will post grant id when created.

marta: adding a follow-up to postmortem: consider making replication put objects with `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id` header explicitly set to dest key — reduce reliance on metadata rewrite.

ash: thanks. keep updates here. If we don't have restore success by EOD escalate to Compliance Slack and Legal channels.
